forces.title: Customer spending prioritises efficiency, automation, productivity gains
forces.description: Customer spending in IT services is becoming highly selective, with budgets increasingly allocated to solutions that offer measurable productivity gains, automation, or enhanced operational efficiency. This structural shift means IT Services & Outsourcing providers must clearly demonstrate tangible value and ROI to secure contracts, moving away from undifferentiated offerings. Firms capable of delivering these outcomes, often leveraging AI, will gain competitive advantage.

forces.title: AI capability emerges as crucial differentiator for IT services
forces.description: The ability to leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a primary differentiator in the IT Services & Outsourcing market. Businesses with strong AI capabilities, particularly in delivering automation and efficiency solutions, are outperforming competitors. This trend drives demand for IT consulting, custom application development, and system integration services focused on AI, creating significant growth opportunities for providers who can translate AI innovation into commercial outcomes.

forces.title: AI-driven cyber threats increase risks and security spending
forces.description: The adoption of AI is simultaneously increasing cyber risks and enabling more frequent, scalable attacks, significantly expanding the digital attack surface. This necessitates higher cybersecurity spending across public and private sectors. For IT Services & Outsourcing firms, this is a key risk as they must secure client systems, but also a significant tailwind, driving demand for advanced cybersecurity consulting, managed security services, and the implementation of AI-powered defense capabilities.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.

forces.title: AI agents transform enterprise operations by orchestrating value chains
forces.description: Agentic AI is moving beyond point solutions to act as intelligent orchestrators across complex enterprise functions like supply chain, procurement, and logistics. This allows for dynamic optimization of entire value chains, rather than isolated processes, leading to improvements in service, cost metrics, and asset utilization. This represents a significant structural change, creating high demand for IT consulting, system integration, and custom application development to design, implement, and manage these advanced AI agent systems for clients.
forces.source_title: The Agentic Leadership Playbook: The COO as Enterprise Orchestrator

forces.title: Regulated industries require common platforms for scalable AI agents
forces.description: For regulated sectors like healthcare and banking, scaling agentic AI demands a common platform of shared standards, reusable capabilities, and consistent controls. This is essential to manage regulatory and operational risks arising from agent autonomy and to ensure interoperability, security, monitoring, and governance. This structural shift drives demand for IT Services & Outsourcing firms specializing in enterprise AI architecture, robust platform development, and integration services that embed guardrails and compliance from inception.
forces.source_title: Building Enterprise AI Agents in Regulated Industries

forces.title: AI set to significantly boost UK labour productivity and GDP
forces.description: Artificial Intelligence is projected to significantly enhance the UK economy, lifting labour productivity by 3.4% over the next decade and contributing a 1.7% impact to total GDP. While this may lead to some employment displacement, the overall effect is a strong economic tailwind. This creates substantial opportunities for IT Services & Outsourcing firms to lead AI implementation, deliver advanced automation solutions, and provide consulting services that help businesses capture these efficiency and growth benefits.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

forces.title: AI evolves to autonomous execution, creating professional-grade digital workers
forces.description: AI has rapidly evolved from an assistive tool to systems capable of autonomous execution, shifting from passive responders to active agents that perform complex tasks with limited supervision. Since 2025, advances in reasoning models and agentic skills have enabled the creation of "professional-grade digital workers." This profound structural change reshapes enterprise operations, creating significant opportunities for IT Services & Outsourcing firms to develop, integrate, and manage these advanced autonomous systems for clients.

forces.title: Shared services evolve into critical AI deployment and scaling platforms
forces.description: Enterprise shared services are transforming from mere transaction factories into crucial AI deployment platforms. They provide the necessary standardized workflows and consolidated data foundations that AI requires to perform effectively and scale efficiently, particularly in regulated industries and during M&A integration. This structural shift creates a strong tailwind for IT Services & Outsourcing firms that can design, implement, and manage these integrated, AI-ready shared services models, expanding their scope to knowledge-based, high-value functions.
forces.source_title: Enterprise Shared Services in Medtech: The Only Wrong Move Is Standing Still

forces.title: New complexity from AI token economics in operational expenditure
forces.description: The rise of AI introduces a new dimension of operational expenditure through "token economics," where costs are dynamic and consumption-driven based on compute usage and model selection. This structural change requires enterprises to manage AI costs by rightsizing models, optimizing consumption, and planning for a dual-cost transition (legacy workforce + AI). IT Services & Outsourcing firms have an opportunity to provide consulting and managed services to help clients establish AI compute budgets, instrument token economics, and optimize model spending for cost efficiency.
forces.source_title: How Token Economics Will Change Opex

forces.title: SaaS vendor data siloing hinders cross-platform AI capabilities
forces.description: A critical headwind for AI transformation is the tendency of some Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) vendors to keep data siloed within their ecosystems, complicating the development of cross-platform AI capabilities. This vendor lock-in strategy can limit organizational flexibility and increase costs for integrating AI agents across various enterprise systems. IT Services & Outsourcing firms face the challenge of advising clients on vendor strategies and building modular, API-driven solutions to mitigate these integration barriers and ensure data fluidity for AI applications.

forces.title: AI governance transitions from manual processes to executable code
forces.description: Traditional, manual risk frameworks for AI deployment are unable to keep pace with the scale of AI adoption. There is a structural shift towards "policy as code," where governance rules are translated into executable code on AI platforms, enabling automated compliance and faster deployment. This creates significant opportunities for IT Services & Outsourcing firms to develop and implement AI governance solutions, embed risk specialists in agile teams, and create risk-differentiated approval paths for clients.

forces.title: Agentic AI necessitates new human accountability and memory management
forces.description: The rise of agentic AI, capable of autonomous actions and multi-agent systems, creates challenges for existing accountability frameworks. The consensus is that accountability must always trace back to a human, requiring new frameworks for delegation and oversight. Furthermore, managing distinct types of agent memory (short-term, long-term, contextual data) presents a novel governance challenge. IT Services & Outsourcing firms can provide critical consulting in developing these frameworks and memory management strategies for clients.

forces.title: Data architecture and governance are core AI capabilities
forces.description: Effective AI implementation critically depends on robust data architecture, governance, and cost management. Much of the enterprise value for AI lies in fragmented, messy, context-rich unstructured data, requiring meticulous classification, metadata, and quality monitoring. Simultaneously, structured data systems face new pressure from high-volume agent queries. This structural change elevates data services – including data readiness, integration, and performance optimization – to a core AI capability for IT Services & Outsourcing providers.

forces.title: Modular AI solutions empower customers, avoiding complexity trap
forces.description: As AI agents become prevalent, the enterprise software industry risks reverting to overly complex, feature-bloated solutions. However, value will increasingly accrue to providers who empower customers with flexible, modular AI solutions rather than complex one-stop offerings. This structural shift demands IT Services & Outsourcing firms to design for adaptability, utilizing composable architectures, clear APIs, and modular services for custom application development and system integration, enabling clients to shape their own AI solutions effectively.
forces.source_title: Agentic AI and the New Complexity Trap in Enterprise Software

forces.title: Reimagining workflows with AI, beyond simple technology layering
forces.description: A significant opportunity for IT Services & Outsourcing is to move beyond simply layering AI technology onto existing, potentially inefficient workflows. Instead, the focus should be on fundamentally reimagining and redesigning work processes with AI from first principles. This approach promises greater organizational impact and value realization, driving demand for strategic IT consulting and process transformation services that integrate AI for optimal outcomes.
forces.source_title: Ushering in the next era of frontline nursing with AI

viewpoints.title: UK Software and IT Services attractive but polarised by differentiation
viewpoints.description: Allianz UK views the UK Software and IT Services sector as fundamentally attractive and growth-oriented, despite increasing market polarisation. Key differentiators for success include scale, recurring revenue models, and strong AI capabilities. Customer spending is more selective, prioritising solutions that deliver measurable productivity gains, automation, and operational efficiency. Providers with clear value propositions and high customer retention are outperforming, whereas less differentiated firms face heightened competition. The long-term outlook remains strong, but the ability to convert innovation into tangible commercial outcomes will be critical for sustained success.

viewpoints.title: Strategic AI adoption drives outperformance in IT services sector
viewpoints.description: Bain & Company highlights that broad AI adoption, when guided by clear strategic priorities, leads to disproportionately strong performance for enterprises. Conversely, fragmented AI initiatives and delayed transformation efforts are rapidly becoming irreversible competitive disadvantages. The increasing velocity of change within AI technologies has established continuous transformation as the new normal for businesses. This dynamic underscores a significant opportunity for IT Services & Outsourcing providers that can help clients implement comprehensive, strategically aligned AI solutions to achieve outsize business outcomes and maintain a competitive edge.

viewpoints.title: AI-driven productivity gains essential but not durable differentiator
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that the "symbiotic enterprise" paradigm, leveraging hybrid human–AI systems, generates significant productivity gains by automating cognitive and physical tasks at lower marginal costs. However, these productivity advantages alone are temporary. As AI capabilities become ubiquitous, such gains will diffuse across industries, becoming a competitive necessity rather than a sustainable differentiator. This implies IT Services & Outsourcing firms must continuously evolve their offerings beyond mere efficiency to help clients embed AI in ways that create deeper, more defensible strategic value, rather than simply focusing on initial cost savings.

demand_drivers.description: AI is projected to boost UK labour productivity by 3.4% over the next decade, with a 1.7% total impact on GDP over the same period. This necessitates substantial investment in AI implementation, custom application development, and system integration, driving demand for IT Services & Outsourcing to facilitate these transformations.

new_opportunities.description: The significant macroeconomic impact of AI on productivity and GDP presents opportunities for IT Services & Outsourcing providers to deliver bespoke AI solutions, integration services, and consulting to help businesses achieve these projected gains. This includes managing AI-driven workforce displacement and ensuring seamless technology adoption.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of the projected impact of AI on the UK economy, including labour productivity and GDP growth over the next decade. No explicit market size figures for IT Services & Outsourcing are provided, but the identified drivers indicate significant market potential.
market_sizing.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites
